title: Belgium vs. France: The Duel Drawing Attention Now
seoTitle: Belgium vs France: Nations League Showdown
subtitle: The Match Decides the Second Round of UEFA Nations League 2026/27 Group A1
excerpt: On Monday, September 28, Belgium will face France at 3:45 PM (local time) at King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels for a crucial encounter.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The encounter between Belgium and France in the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 is drawing attention as it takes place on Monday, September 28, at 3:45 PM, at King Baudouin Stadium in Brussels. The duel is part of the second round of Group A1, where both national teams won their opening matches, and it influences qualification for Euro 2028 and the European playoff round for the 2030 World Cup Qualifiers.

Belgium Seeks Continuity

Belgium, under the command of Mark van Bommel, enters the match as group leader, having defeated Italy 2-0 at Rome's Olympic Stadium. The coach emphasized the need to maintain intensity and work ethic, and he expects Godts to start on the left side of the attack, with Ngoy and Mechele forming the central defensive pairing.

France Without Its Key Striker

The French national team, led by Zinédine Zidane, will be without Kylian Mbappé, who suffered a left knee injury in the victory over Turkey. The coach anticipates that Doué will take his place in the attacking trio, alongside Dembélé and Olise, and mentioned that there will be squad rotation due to the short interval between matches.

Impact on the Group Stage

The Nations League group stage runs until November 17 this year, and the best performances will lead national teams to the quarter-final phase, scheduled for March 25-30, 2027. Group A1, where Belgium and France compete, already features Italy and Turkey as close rivals, who will also face each other on the same afternoon.

Where to Watch and Times

The match can be followed live on ESPN and Disney+ platforms, in addition to being broadcast in Real-Time on ge. The main highlights are available on the ge platform, and fans can follow the match at Brasília time, which corresponds to 3:45 PM.

Full Match Schedule

In addition to Belgium vs. France, Monday features Turkey vs. Italy, both at 3:45 PM, and other lower-tier UEFA Nations League group matches, such as Georgia vs. Ukraine, Armenia vs. Montenegro, and Latvia vs. Cyprus, which kick off at 1:00 PM. In Brazil, Série B concludes the round with América-MG vs. Juventude, at 7:30 PM, on Disney+.

With information from ge, VEJA.
